tests.name: the message as git would write it > joins repeated -m as paragraphs, as git does
tests.why: new parser module; checks repeated -m joined the git way

tests.name: the message as git would write it > does not read -F outside the folder, through a link, or after a cd
tests.why: the -F outside-folder case and its card note

tests.name: the message as git would write it > shows each commit in a chain, and ignores near-misses beside them
tests.why: commits inside && and ; chains plus near-miss commands

tests.name: the owner's commit rules > say nothing about a clean message, or a subject alone
tests.why: clean message and subject-only show no rule lines

tests.name: the owner's commit rules > list every rule broken, one line each
tests.why: all rules broken at once, one line each

tests.name: the owner's commit rules > flag a process story
tests.why: one rule broken alone (process story); sibling tests cover the others

tests.name: the commit card's answers > shows the message and its rule breaks, offers only once, edits by rejection, and approves the re-issued commit
tests.why: approve once, edit then re-issue, empty edit refused, through SessionManager and the fake engine

tests.name: the commit card's answers > sends the edited text fenced, after the exact instruction
tests.why: rejection feedback carries the fixed instruction and fenced text

tests.name: the commit card's answers > denies like any other card
tests.why: deny path; relies on a fake-engine phrase the branch adds

tests.name: no approval but the owner's passes a commit > auto-approve passes other commands but waits on a commit, and on a commit beside a sandbox bypass
tests.why: autoApprove session and sandbox-bypass commit both wait for the owner

tests.name: no approval but the owner's passes a commit > an analysis session's auto-approval waits on a commit
the worktree's edge: symlinks and parent paths count as outside, ordinary commands as inside
tests.why: existing test gained asserts that a commit stays outside a task's approval; base already refused it

tests.name: a commit card and the turn's end > Stop answers an open commit card, and a later answer to it is refused
tests.why: Stop rejecting an open card is existing card behaviour; note the test's setup uses a fake phrase added by the branch

tests.name: a commit card and the turn's end > a commit request that arrives after Stop waits for the owner and answers only itself, even with auto-approve
tests.why: late commit after Stop with auto-approve would be approved on base

tests.name: a commit card and the turn's end > a host restart with a commit card open leaves it unanswerable, so it cannot approve into a later turn
tests.why: host-restart order; title quotes the MUST's approve-into-a-later-turn wording; base cards already behaved so

tests: tests/unit/task-loop.test.ts::the worktree's edge: symlinks and parent paths count as outside, ordinary commands as inside
tests/unit/commit-card.test.ts::no approval but the owner's passes a commit > auto-approve passes other commands but waits on a commit, and on a commit beside a sandbox bypass
findings.note: The task case is only checked on the inside() predicate, not through a task-role session's permission path. A test that fails on base would not expose this: base already refused commits for tasks, so only a PASS_TO_PASS test through a real task session would cover it.

notes: The which-commands-are-commits it.each table was skipped because its titles are printf-formatted. tests/e2e/app.spec.ts also covers MUST 1-3 in Playwright (show, edit, re-issue, approve). No test cites a MUST by number; only one test title quotes MUST wording. FAIL_TO_PASS vs PASS_TO_PASS for MUST 5 is inferred: that MUST asks for today's card behaviour, but some of its tests depend on fake-engine phrases that exist only on the branch.
